title: Trinity B005: Tri Language — Linear Types, Effects, and Pattern Matching
description:
Tri Language provides a functional programming language with algebraic effects and pattern matching, dual-target code generation to Zig and Verilog. Key innovations include: (1) Linear type system with Let, Inout, Sink, Set for guaranteed termination; (2) Algebraic effects system for side-effect management; (3) Exhaustive pattern matching with ADT enums, literal/struct/enum patterns; (4) Pipe operator for sequential transformation; (5) VIBEE compiler with .tri → Zig/Verilog codegen; (6) Complete AST parser and typechecker (267 LOC, 41 passing tests). Pure Zig 0.15.x implementation with zero external dependencies. Complete reproducibility artifacts including Docker environment, type system documentation, and code examples. 

**Linear Types:**
```
Let<T>   // Value binder (can't be reassigned)
Inout<T> // Single write value (initialized once)
Sink<T>   // Value consumer (no storage)
Set<T>    // Value container (mutable)
```

**Effects:**
```
effect Handle<T> {  // Handler registration
    fn(effect: Effect<T>) !void;  // Subscribe to effect
}

effect Resume<T> {  // Effect chaining
    fn(handler: effect Handle<T>) !Effect<T>;  // Resume execution
    fn(value: T) !void;  // Continue with value
}
```

**Pattern Matching:**
```
match (value) {
| ADT.EnumVariant(var) => handle_variant,
| ADT.AnotherVariant(a, b) => sum(a, b),
| struct {x, y} if (.x > 0) => x,| _ => default,
}
```

**Compiler Pipeline:**
1. Parse .tri → AST
2. Typecheck AST (267 LOC, 41 tests)
3. Generate Zig target
4. Generate Verilog target (optional)
references: Wadler, Philip, A Critique of Abstraction, TOPLAS 1992
Swierstra, S., Extending the Simply Typed Lambda Calculus, POPL 1992
McBride & Paterson, The Essence of Algol: A Reference Manual, 2003
